RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the July 27, 2006/Sravana 5, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; External Affairs; Housing and Urban Poverty
Alleviation; Information and Broadcasting; Overseas Indian Affairs;
Panchayati Raj; Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances
and Pensions; Planning; Shipping, Road Transport and Highways;
Space; Statistics and Programme Implementation; Urban
Development; Youth Affairs and Sports )
Total number of questions —20
Safeguard agreement with IAEA
*61. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the draft Bill on the US and
India Nuclear Cooperation Promotion Act
of 2006 states that the US President must
first determine that India and the
International Atomic Energy Agency
(IAEA) have concluded safeguards
agreements requiring the application of
IAEA safeguards in perpetuity; and
(b) if so, the reaction of Government on
this which runs completely contrary to the
assurance given by the Prime Minister in
both Houses of Parliament that India would
approach the IAEA for safeguards only after
USA endorses the July 18, 2005 nuclear
deal?
Sports infrastructure in rural areas
*62. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND
SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is acute
shortage of sports infrastructure facilities
in rural areas;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps taken to start an effective programme
for youth of rural areas; and
(c) the details of the schemes under
which financial assistance is provided for
the promotion of sports in the country
through NGOs and performance review of
such schemes, particularly in Maharashtra
State?

20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Consultative Committees
†*63. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is compulsory to
constitute ‘Consultative Committees’ for
all Ministries;
(b) if so, the names of Ministries under
the present Government functioning since
May, 2004 where ‘Consultative
Committees’ have not been constituted so
far and the reasons therefor; and
(c)  by when the Committees are likely
to be constituted?
Placing of India on “Watch List” by US
*64. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Annual
Report 2006 of the States Department of
the United States has categorized India as
the source, destination, and transit country
for men, women and children trafficked for
the purposes of forced or bonded labour
and commercial sexual exploitation and
have placed our country in the “Watch List”;
(b) if so, the details of Government’s
response, if any, conveyed to the US thereto;
(c)  the basis of the said response; and
(d) the implications of a country being
placed in the “Watch List” by the US
administration?
Stricter Visa regulations in developed
Countries
*65. SHRI SHANTARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Visa regulations in
developed countries have been made
stricter in recent times;
(b) whether the development has
affected Indians proposing to visit these
countries on different types of Visas;
(c)  if so, whether Government have
made any representation with the
Government of these countries in this
regard; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Corporatisation of major ports
*66. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to corporatise all the major ports in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c)  whether a foreign consultancy firm
has been engaged to advise Government in
this regard; and
(d) if so, what are its findings and
recommendations and the targeted date for
finalizing the issue?
Role of Gram Sabhas
*67. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of
PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:
(a) the role of the Gram Sabhas in
implementing various schemes for helping
the poor;
(b) whether it is a fact that Gram Sabhas
are being neglected and not encouraged to
function; and

(c)  if so, the remedial measures planned
to make the Gram Sabhas effective?
Requests for Kuwait war compensation
*68. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the details of requests for the Kuwait
war compensation from the large number
of people from Kerala;
(b) whether Government have requested
to the United Nations Compensation
Commission to extend the prescribed time
limit for the submission of applications;
and
(c)  if so, the details thereof?

Total number of questions — 143
Setting up of new nuclear plants
256. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up
more nuclear plants following Indo-U.S.
deal;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Nuclear plants in West Bengal and
Orissa
257. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to locate a
nuclear plant in West Bengal;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the norms that have been laid down
for setting up such plants in the country;
(d) whether such a plant is also
proposed to be located in the backward
State of Orissa; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Uranium plants in Maharashtra and
Chhattisgarh
258. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to set up a Uranium processing
plant in Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh; and
(b) if so, by when it is likely to be set
up?
Addition to nuclear energy capacity
259. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Planning

62
Commission has accepted a
recommendation to raise India's nuclear
energy capacity to 1,00,000 MW in 25
years; and
(b) if so, the details of the proposal?
Additional generation of electricity
260. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the annual generation of electricity
by each Nuclear Power Plant during the
last three years, year-wise and plant-wise;
(b) the expected additional generation
of electricity from each plant during the
period 2006-07 and 2007-08; and
(c) the extent to which the demand of
the country shall be met as a result of such
generation of electricity particularly in Uttar
Pradesh?
Opening up of coal sector to private
sector investments
261. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are taking measures to remove the control
that the CIL is enjoying with regard to
supply of coal to domestic consumers;
(b) if so, whether it is a part of the
move in view of Government's decision to
amend the Coal (Nationalization) Act, to
open up coal sector to private sector
investments;
(c) the total number of coal blocks in
the country with CIL and the production
of coal in these blocks during the last 5
years, year-wise and State-wise; and
(d) the reasons for (a) above and
whether any political consensus have been
arrived at with regard to (b) above?
Production and supply of coal
262. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) the present stage of production and
supply of coal by Coal India Ltd. during
the last three years;
(b) whether CIL has developed any new
mining areas to increase coal production
during the above-mentioned period; and
(c) if so, the plans of CIL to increase
production in order to meet the
requirements of industries for power
generation?
Monopoly in coal supply
263. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SYEDA
ANWARA TAIMUR:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have initiated
the process of loosening Coal India
Limited's virtual monopoly in supplying
coal to domestic consumers and also
allowed a slew of State Government owned
companies to not only undertake coal
mining in some blocks but also allow them
to sell to non-captive consumers;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when the proposal is likely to be
implemented?
Tribal land taken for coal excavation
in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh
264. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the number of acres of tribal land
that have been taken by his Ministry for

63
coal excavation in Jharkhand and
Chhattisgarh, district-wise, block-wise,
panchayat-wise, during the last five years;
(b) the details of the rehabilitation
package that is offered to the tribals who
are affected and displaced by coal mining
in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh; and
(c) whether the coal companies give
displaced tribals employment, if so, how
many have been given employment and if
not, the plan to compensate them?

mining blocks
